s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive ocular and musculoskeletal abnormalities with onset in adolescence
salient_findings: Hypermobility of shoulders, digits, and knees
Substantial optic nerve cupping and loss of neural rim tissue
key_facts: Age of onset: 13 years
Elevated intraocular pressure
Taller stature than relatives
Long fingers
Hypermobility of shoulders, digits, and knees
Family history negative for similar findings
Normal serial echocardiograms
Open iridocorneal angle in each eye
No Haab striae, buphthalmos, or high iris insertion
Subtle lens dislocation superonasally in the right eye at age 17
Lens dislocation in the left eye at age 32
Genetic testing revealed 2 heterozygous variants in the LTBP2 gene

shortlist.label: Homocystinuria
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated intraocular pressure, lens dislocation, and hypermobility are consistent with this condition

shortlist.label: Weill-Marchesani syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by ectopia lentis, glaucoma, and musculoskeletal abnormalities, matching the patient's presentation

shortlist.label: Marfan syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Features such as tall stature, long fingers, and lens dislocation are typical of this condition

shortlist.label: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Hypermobility and musculoskeletal findings are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: LTBP2-related glaucoma
shortlist.why_kept: Genetic testing revealed variants in the LTBP2 gene, which is associated with glaucoma and matches the patient's ocular findings

raw.rationale: The presence of elevated intraocular pressure, open iridocorneal angle, and lens dislocation, combined with the genetic testing revealing 2 heterozygous variants in the LTBP2 gene, strongly supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Homocystinuria
rejected.why: Typically associated with mental retardation, thromboembolism, and other systemic features not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Weill-Marchesani syndrome
rejected.why: Characterized by short stature, brachydactyly, and joint stiffness, which contradicts the patient's tall stature and hypermobility

rejected.label: Marfan syndrome
rejected.why: Typically involves cardiac abnormalities, such as aortic root dilatation, which is not present in this patient

rejected.label: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
rejected.why: While hypermobility is a feature, the absence of skin hyperextensibility, fragility, or other typical features makes this diagnosis less likely
